source: phase2-web-extraction workflow (7 mappers + adversarial critique; spot-check found 0 wrong endpoints)

map.area: Heartbeat / presence + NowPlayingElsewhere (multi-device playback awareness & cross-device resume) in AURA web

files.role: Client heartbeat + poll hook. Constants HEARTBEAT_MS=20000, POLL_MS=20000. Beats while playing (immediately + every 20s + on track-id/play-state change), one 'stopped' beat on pause (guarded by hasPlayed ref so a cold-boot idle mount never overwrites the device's real last-playback row with a progress-0 beat), keepalive 'stopped' beat on window pagehide. Polls /api/playback/now every 20s only while document is visible (skips when document.hidden, re-ticks on visibilitychange). Returns othersPlaying array. All gated on isAuthed().

API wrappers: sendHeartbeat (POST /api/playback/heartbeat, supports fetch keepalive:true for unload), getNowPlaying (GET /api/playback/now -> playing[] or [] on any error), getResume (GET /api/playback/resume -> resume or null). All best-effort; every failure is swallowed so awareness never disrupts playback.

Passive banner UI. Shows only devices[0] (most recent other device): pulsing dot + 'Playing “Title” on <deviceLabel>' + dismiss X. Dismiss key is `${deviceLabel}|${track.id}` so a new song on the same device re-surfaces it. Awareness only: no pause, no takeover, no control of the other device.

Styling for BOTH banners (.aura-npe shared by NPE and the resume offer). Fixed top-center pill (top:14px, z-index 60), slide-in keyframe, pulsing accent dot keyframe, :hover states on action/dismiss buttons, prefers-reduced-motion override. .aura-npe--resume moves the resume banner to top:60px so it stacks below the NPE note when both show.

Wiring. Line 533: othersPlaying = usePlaybackPresence({track, playing, progress}) — progress is the 0-1 fraction from the player 'progress' event (line 845-849). Lines 552-578: cross-device resume — one-shot getResume() on mount, offers only if fresh (<24h), 0.02<progress<0.98, and track differs from BOTH the locally saved position's trackId and the currently loaded track; acceptResume() writes savePosition(trackId, fraction)+flushPosition() then pickLiveTrack(track) (the track-load effect auto-seeks to the saved fraction). Lines 1678-1688: renders <NowPlayingElsewhere devices={othersPlaying}/> and the resume banner ('Pick up “Title” from your other device?' with Resume + dismiss buttons).

localStorage 'aura.position' = {trackId, progress(0-1)} with a 5s debounced write + flush(). Resume-accept writes through this so the load effect seeks; also used to compare 'is the other device's track different from my saved spot'.

Routes (lines 592-621): POST /api/playback/heartbeat, GET /api/playback/now, GET /api/playback/resume — all requireAuth, cheap DB-only, covered by the app-wide generalLimiter (600 req / 5 min per key on /api), NOT the LLM cost limiter.

Server logic. recordHeartbeat(sessionId, userId, {track,isPlaying,progress}): updates the caller's OWN user_sessions row (playing_track JSONB, is_playing, position_sec=0-1 clamped fraction, playing_at=last_seen_at=now); string clamps id<=200/title<=300/artist<=200/imageUrl<=1000; silent no-op when sessionId is null (legacy no-sid tokens don't participate). FRESH_MS=60000: a session counts as 'currently playing' only while its heartbeat is <60s old. getNowPlaying(userId, currentSid): other non-revoked sessions with is_playing=TRUE and playing_at>now-60s, excluding caller's sid, newest first. getResume(userId, currentSid): single most-recent other-session row with playing_track NOT NULL, position_sec>0.02, playing_at>now-24h.

Identity plumbing the feature rides on. Session id 'ses_'+18 random bytes (base64url), carried as `sid` claim in the 30-day HS256 JWT; requireAuth/resolveSession set req.sessionId (null for grandfathered pre-session tokens). Token read from httpOnly aura_session cookie (SameSite=Strict) FIRST, then Authorization: Bearer fallback (the native path). Separate persistent-device cookie aura_device='dev_'+random (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, ~400-day rolling) — NOT auth, used only for new-device email alerts, stored as user_sessions.device_id. deviceLabel(ua) parses User-Agent server-side into 'Chrome · Windows' style ('Unknown device' fallback) — this is the string the NPE banner shows. last_seen_at bumped on any authed request, throttled to 5 min.

Session creation: startSession -> ensureDeviceId + createSessionWithCap (hard cap MAX_ACTIVE_SESSIONS=env MAX_DEVICES||3; 403 code 'device_limit' returns the sessions list + limit; retry with evictSessionId). sessionPayload: web gets only {user} (JWT stays in the httpOnly cookie); a client sending header X-Aura-Client: native gets the SAME JWT in the response body ({user, token}) for Bearer use. Device endpoints: GET /api/auth/sessions, DELETE /api/auth/sessions/:id, DELETE /api/auth/sessions?scope=others.

Migration v17_user_sessions creates the table that doubles as the per-device now-playing registry (no separate table, no push channel): id, user_id, device_label, user_agent, ip, city, country, created_at, last_seen_at, revoked_at, playing_track JSONB, is_playing BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE, playing_at BIGINT, position_sec REAL; partial index on user_id WHERE revoked_at IS NULL. v21 adds device_id TEXT.

endpoints.purpose: Playing device reports its current track/state into its own user_sessions row (identified by the JWT's sid). Sent every 20s while playing, plus on track change, play/pause, and pagehide (keepalive 'stopped' beat).
endpoints.params: Auth: aura_session cookie or Authorization: Bearer <jwt> (token must carry sid, else server no-ops). JSON body: { track: { id (<=200 ch), title (<=300), artist (<=200), imageUrl (<=1000) } | null, isPlaying: boolean, progress: number 0-1 fraction (clamped server-side) }
endpoints.responseShape: 200 { ok: true }; 401 { error: 'invalid token' }; 5xx { error: string }. Note: a no-sid legacy token still gets { ok: true } but nothing is recorded.

endpoints.purpose: Poll: which of MY OTHER devices are currently playing (fresh heartbeat <60s + is_playing=TRUE, non-revoked, caller's own session excluded). Client polls every 20s while visible; drives the NowPlayingElsewhere banner.
endpoints.params: Auth cookie/Bearer only; no query params. Caller's sid (from the JWT) is what gets excluded.
endpoints.responseShape: 200 { playing: [ { deviceLabel: string|null (UA-derived, e.g. 'Chrome · Windows'), track: { id, title, artist, imageUrl } | null, since: number (epoch ms of last heartbeat) } ] } ordered newest-first (client UI only uses [0]); 401/5xx { error: string }

endpoints.purpose: Cross-device 'continue where you left off': most recent real playback on the user's OTHER devices. Fetched once on app mount; drives the 'Pick up “Title” from your other device?' banner.
endpoints.params: Auth cookie/Bearer only; no query params. Server filters: other sessions only, playing_track NOT NULL, position_sec > 0.02, playing_at within 24h, LIMIT 1 by playing_at DESC.
endpoints.responseShape: 200 { resume: { track: { id, title, artist, imageUrl }, progress: number 0-1 fraction (NOT seconds, despite the position_sec column name), at: number (epoch ms) } | null }; 401/5xx { error: string }. Client additionally requires progress < 0.98 and track different from local saved spot before offering.

endpoints.purpose: Adjacent: device list backing Settings; same user_sessions rows the heartbeat writes into. Useful to the native app for the device-limit UX.
endpoints.responseShape: 200 { sessions: [ { id, deviceLabel, city, country, createdAt (ms), lastSeenAt (ms) } ] (last_seen DESC, active <30d, non-revoked), currentId: string (caller's sid), limit: number }

endpoints.purpose: Adjacent: revoke one device session (kills its token + removes it from presence, since getNowPlaying filters revoked_at IS NULL).
endpoints.responseShape: 2xx on success; error { error: string } otherwise

endpoints.purpose: Adjacent: log out all other devices, keeping the caller's session.
endpoints.responseShape: 2xx on success

endpoints.purpose: Adjacent but critical for native: the only places a session (sid) is minted. Presence is keyed by that sid.
endpoints.params: Standard credential bodies plus optional evictSessionId (drop a device when at the cap). NATIVE: send header X-Aura-Client: native to receive the JWT in the body.
endpoints.responseShape: 200 { user } for web, { user, token } when X-Aura-Client: native; 403 { code: 'device_limit', limit, sessions: [...] } at the 3-device cap (retry with evictSessionId)

components.name: usePlaybackPresence (hook)
components.purpose: Single client entry point for presence: heartbeats this device's playback and polls for the user's other playing devices.
behaviors: Heartbeat every 20s while playing, plus immediate beat on track-id or play-state change (effect deps [track?.id, playing])
Reads track/playing/progress from a ref so the interval never re-binds on ~1/s progress ticks
One isPlaying:false beat on pause/stop, only after this device has actually played (hasPlayed ref) — prevents a cold-boot idle mount clobbering the resume row with progress 0
pagehide listener sends a keepalive:true 'stopped' beat so it survives tab close/unload
Polls /api/playback/now every 20s; skips while document.hidden; immediate re-tick on visibilitychange to visible
Everything no-ops when not authed; all network errors swallowed
components.visualSpec: None (headless hook); returns othersPlaying: [{deviceLabel, track, since}]

components.name: NowPlayingElsewhere
components.purpose: Passive dismissible note that the user is also playing on another device. Pure awareness — it does NOT pause local playback, does NOT offer to take over or transfer playback, and has no control over the remote device.
behaviors: Renders only devices[0] (most recent other playing device); null when list empty
Text: 'Playing “<title>” on <deviceLabel>' with 'another device' fallback when deviceLabel is missing; title omitted when absent
Dismiss X hides it for the current deviceLabel+trackId pair (local component state, not persisted) — a new track or different device re-surfaces it
Self-clears within ~60s of the other device stopping (server freshness window) + up to 20s poll latency
role=status for screen readers
components.visualSpec: Fixed pill, top:14px centered (translateX(-50%)), z-index 60, max-width min(92vw,460px), border-radius 999px, surface bg + 1px line border + soft shadow, 12.5px text, 7px pulsing accent dot (1.8s opacity keyframe), 240ms slide-in animation, 20px round dismiss button with :hover color change, prefers-reduced-motion disables both animations

components.name: Resume offer banner (inline JSX in App.jsx, no dedicated component)
components.purpose: Cross-device resume: on cold boot, offer to pick up a track another device was recently playing. This is the ONLY 'take over'-adjacent behavior, and it is pull-based (start playing here) — it never stops the other device.
behaviors: getResume() exactly once on mount (empty-dep effect)
Offer shown only if: resume.at < 24h old, 0.02 < progress < 0.98, track.id differs from localStorage-saved position's trackId AND from the currently loaded track
Resume button: saves {trackId, progress-fraction} via savePosition + flushPosition (so the track-load effect auto-seeks), then pickLiveTrack(track) starts playback locally
Dismiss X just clears the offer state (no persistence — reappears on next cold boot if still eligible)
Reuses .aura-npe styling; adds .aura-npe--resume (top:60px) when othersPlaying is non-empty so both banners stack
components.visualSpec: Same pill as NowPlayingElsewhere plus an accent-colored 'Resume' action button (border-radius 999px, 12px/600 text, :hover opacity 0.92); sits at top:60px when the NPE note is also visible, else top:14px

stateAndStorage: Server: user_sessions row per login doubles as the per-device now-playing registry (migration v17) — playing_track JSONB {id,title,artist,imageUrl}, is_playing BOOLEAN, playing_at BIGINT (ms), position_sec REAL holding a 0-1 FRACTION (column name is misleading), plus device_label/user_agent/ip/city/country/created_at/last_seen_at/revoked_at/device_id. Heartbeat updates playing_* and last_seen_at together.

Freshness model: 'currently playing' = is_playing AND playing_at within 60s (FRESH_MS); resume eligibility = playing_track set, position_sec>0.02, playing_at within 24h. No push channel anywhere — pure poll.

Client localStorage 'aura.position' = {trackId, progress(0-1)}, written via 5s-debounced savePosition/flush (src/lib/persistPosition.js); the resume handoff writes through it so the existing load-effect seek path does the seeking.

Client React state only: othersPlaying (hook state), dismissed key (NPE component state, per device+track, session-lifetime), resumeOffer (App state, one-shot). Nothing presence-related is persisted client-side.

Cookies: aura_session (httpOnly, SameSite=Strict, 30d) carries the JWT whose sid keys the heartbeat row; aura_device (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, ~400d rolling, 'dev_...') is a NON-auth device recognizer for new-device emails only — presence does NOT use it; presence identity is per-login sid, so two browsers on one physical device count as two 'devices'.
Hard cap: max 3 active sessions (env MAX_DEVICES); revoked/expired rows drop out of presence automatically (revoked_at IS NULL + created_at window filters).
portingNotes: Heartbeat must move out of the UI layer: the web hook lives in React and relies on the tab being alive. On native, playback continues with the app backgrounded/killed-UI, so the 20s heartbeat should be driven by the playback service (RNTP event/progress loop in the foreground service), not a mounted component. Payload/endpoint stay identical.

pagehide + fetch keepalive (the 'stopped' beat on tab close) is web-only. Native equivalents: send isPlaying:false on pause/stop/queue-ended events and on app termination if catchable; otherwise rely on the server's 60s freshness window — a killed app just fades out of 'now playing' within a minute (server already designed for this).

document.hidden / visibilitychange gating of the /now poll is web-only — map to AppState ('active' resumes polling, background stops it). Polling in background is pointless anyway since the banner is UI.

Auth: the aura_session httpOnly cookie won't ride RN fetches. Server already supports the native path end-to-end: send X-Aura-Client: native on login/google/verify-otp to get the JWT in the response body, store it (MMKV), send Authorization: Bearer on every call. CRITICAL: the token carries the sid; without a sid the heartbeat silently no-ops (recordHeartbeat returns early) — so never mint tokens outside the session-creating endpoints.

deviceLabel is derived SERVER-side from the User-Agent at login (deviceLabel() in server/middleware/auth.js). RN's default UA (okhttp/...) matches none of the browser regexes -> the native device will show as 'Unknown device' in everyone's NPE banners and device lists. Either send a crafted UA containing 'Android' at login (yields just 'Android') or add a small server change / header for a proper label like 'AURA · Android'.

progress is a 0-1 FRACTION everywhere (heartbeat body, resume response, the position_sec DB column despite its name, localStorage aura.position). RNTP thinks in seconds — convert fraction*duration on resume-seek and position/duration on send.

Resume accept on web is indirect: it writes localStorage then lets the existing track-load effect auto-seek. Native must implement the direct version: load track, seek to fraction*duration, play. Also replicate the local guards (offer only if <24h, 0.02<p<0.98, differs from local last-position track and current track) and keep a native equivalent of the persisted last-position store (MMKV) for the comparison.

UI is web-idiomatic: fixed-position CSS pill with keyframe slide-in, pulsing-dot animation, :hover states on the action/dismiss buttons, prefers-reduced-motion media query, and a hardcoded top:60px stacking hack when both banners show. Rethink as native toasts/snackbars or a queue-screen inline row; hover states need press/ripple equivalents; the stacking should become a proper banner queue.
Dismiss state is in-memory per component ('deviceLabel|trackId' key) — intentionally re-surfaces on new track and on app restart. Cheap to keep identical.

There is NO playback takeover/transfer/remote-control anywhere: the server never pushes, other devices are never paused, and the only cross-device action is pull-based resume on cold boot. If native wants Spotify-Connect-style transfer, that's new server work, not a port.
Rate limits are generous for this traffic (600 req/5min general limiter; heartbeat+poll = ~6 req/min) — no native throttling changes needed if the 20s cadences are kept.

Because presence is keyed by per-login session (sid), the native app will appear as its own 'device' alongside browser sessions and counts toward the 3-session cap — handle the 403 device_limit response (show sessions list, let user pick evictSessionId, retry) in the native login flow.

map.area: AURA web search — pre-query trending/recents sidebar + categorized live search (mobile "headerless" variant of DesktopSearch under the morphing MobileTopBar)

files.role: Pre-query sidebar: 'recent' chips (with clear) + 'trending' chips. TRENDING_BY_LANG is a HARDCODED module constant — 6 query strings per language key (all/tamil/english/hindi/malayalam/kannada; any other language pill falls back to 'all'). No endpoint, no refresh cadence — it changes only on deploy. Tapping a chip calls onPick(query).

The search screen (shared desktop+mobile; `headerless` prop = mobile). Owns lang pills, debounced fetch, result sections (top hero / songs / artists / albums&movies / playlists / your playlists), idle/loading/error/nothing states, per-song overflow menu, scroll memory, BackToTop, and renders SearchSidebar.

Layout: grid 1fr + 240px sticky sidebar at >=1100px, single column below; @container dse (max-width:600px) mobile tightening (2-col tile grid, 22px gutters, sidebar goes static and stacks BELOW results); hover-reveal rules for the per-tile more-button; screen enter (460ms) / exit (320ms) animations for mobile search open/close.

Mobile search entry: top pill morphs into the search field (two inert-toggled layers). Owns the input on mobile (screen is input-less), synchronous focus inside the opening tap for iOS keyboard, blur-collapse-when-empty logic with pointerdown capture tracking, clear + back buttons. Placeholder: 'search a song, artist, or mood…'.

Frontend client. searchCatalog(query,{lang,langs,limit,signal}) -> GET /api/catalog/search; getAlbum -> GET /api/albums/:id; getTrack -> GET /api/catalog/track/:id; getFeatured -> GET /api/catalog/featured (home, not search).

Route handlers. /api/catalog/search (lines 141-209): parallel searchSongs + searchSuggest + searchPlaylists, album name-match-first + language ranking, album-hero promotion, artist row gating (top not artist, name contains query, cap 5). Also /api/catalog/track/:id, /api/albums/:id, /api/artists/lookup, /api/catalog/featured.

Upstream provider access: searchSongs (song search, dedupe by title|artist, optional lang filter), searchSuggest (autocomplete: top/artists/albums/playlists, 80-entry LRU per query), mapSong shape {id,title,artist,album,language,durationSec,streamUrl(decrypted CDN),imageUrl,explicit}, rankByLang. getCatalogHome's new_trending bucket exists but only feeds discover.js — NOT exposed as any trending endpoint.

searchPlaylists(userId,q,{limit:5}) — user's owned OR collaborated playlists matched by name ILIKE or contained track title/artist ILIKE, ORDER BY updated_at DESC; returns {id,name,trackCount,coverImageUrl,...}.
Recents store: module-scope singleton mirrored to localStorage 'aura.recentSearches', cap 10, newest-first, case-insensitive dedupe; pushRecentSearch / clearRecentSearches / useRecentSearches.
Module-scope shared query store (top-bar field and search screen read/write the same value; survives screen unmount). No persistence.
Module-scope result cache: Map keyed `query|lang`, 12-entry LRU-ish (re-insert on set), plus lastLang persistence for the language pill (in-memory only).
Focus event bus with a buffered pending flag — '/' shortcut or openSearch requests focus before the input exists; subscriber picks it up post-mount.
Plain 300ms setTimeout debounce used on the query.

Canonical language list: PRIMARY = tamil, english, hindi, malayalam, kannada, telugu; MORE = bengali, marathi, punjabi, gujarati, urdu, bhojpuri, odia, assamese. Search pills = ['all', ...LANGUAGES] (15 pills total).
dropExplicit(list, on) — client-side Family-mode filter applied only to the songs section (other sections carry no per-track flag).
getSeedSignals() reads the user's priority-ordered languages from localStorage — becomes the `langs` param for my-languages-first ranking.
Global track menu bus: toggleTrackMenu({track,x,y}) from the per-song overflow button; base actions play/playNext/addToQueue/addToPlaylist/like/artist; long-press support on touch.

Wiring: openSearch/closeSearch (remembers return screen, 320ms exit sync with top-bar collapse, clears query on close), passes headerless={isMobile} + familyMode + onPickLive (play track) + navigation handlers; '/' hotkey -> navigate to search + requestSearchFocus.

Auth: httpOnly cookie 'aura_session' (web) OR Authorization: Bearer <jwt> fallback — native clients get the same JWT in the login response body when sending X-Aura-Client: native (server/auth.js line 61).

endpoints.purpose: The one search endpoint — categorized results in a single call. optionalAuth (userPlaylists only when a valid session/Bearer rides along). Fires on every 300ms-debounced keystroke; client aborts stale requests via AbortController. NOTE: there is NO trending endpoint — pre-query trending is a hardcoded client list.
endpoints.params: q (required, non-empty; else 400 {error:'missing query'}) · lang (optional exact language filter; web omits it for the 'all' pill) · langs (optional comma-separated user languages in priority order; drives my-languages-first ranking of albums, and of songs only when the top result is an album) · limit (Number, default 20; web sends 12; songs upstream cap 40)
endpoints.responseShape: { top: null | {type:'song'|'album'|'artist'|'playlist', id, name, image, isMovie?}, songs: [{id, title, artist, album, language, durationSec, streamUrl (decrypted, playable CDN mp4 URL), imageUrl, explicit:boolean}] (deduped by lowered title|artist), artists: [{id, name, image}] (max 5; ONLY present when top isn't an artist AND the name contains the query, query>=2 chars), albums: [{id, name, image, year, language, isMovie:boolean, subtitle}] (max 12; sorted name-match-first, then user-language, then catalog order; when suggest's top is an album the ranked albums[0] is promoted into `top` and removed from the list), playlists: [{id, name, image, subtitle:'AURA'}] (max 12, catalog editorial), userPlaylists: [{id, name, trackCount, coverImageUrl}] (max 5, signed-in only; matches playlist name OR a contained track's title/artist, owned or collaborated, newest-updated first) }. Errors: 400 missing query; song-search failure -> {error} with upstream status hidden (502); suggest/userPlaylists failures degrade to empty buckets, never error.

endpoints.purpose: Single-track detail (fresh streamUrl); used when rehydrating a picked track.
endpoints.responseShape: Track object: {id, title, artist, album, language, durationSec, streamUrl, imageUrl, explicit} (or {error} with err.statusCode)

endpoints.purpose: Album/movie detail — target of album tiles and an album-type top-result hero.
endpoints.responseShape: { album: {id, name, image, year, artist, subtitle, isMovie, tracks: Track[]} }

endpoints.purpose: Artist detail — target of artist tiles and an artist-type top-result hero (artist screen fetches by id).
endpoints.params: name OR id OR trackId (query string, all optional selectors)
endpoints.responseShape: { artist: {...} } (or {error})

endpoints.purpose: NOT part of the search screen (home shelf, mode-seeded). Listed because it is the closest thing to server-side 'trending' the API exposes; the upstream new_trending bucket (getCatalogHome) only feeds the discover pool internally and has no route of its own.
endpoints.responseShape: { results: Track[] }

components.name: SearchSidebar (recents + trending)
components.purpose: Everything the user sees before typing (besides the idle hint), and it stays visible next to/below results while searching.
behaviors: Trending source = TRENDING_BY_LANG[lang] ?? TRENDING_BY_LANG.all — static, in-bundle, per-language (only all/tamil/english/hindi/malayalam/kannada have curated lists; telugu + the 8 'more' languages fall back to 'all'). Zero network, zero refresh cadence.
Heading reads 'trending' or 'trending · {lang}' when a specific language pill is active — trending follows the pill instantly.
Tapping a chip sets the shared search query; on mobile it also fires requestSearchFocus() so the top-bar input refocuses and the keyboard reopens (the screen itself has no input).
Recents section: 'recent' heading + 'clear' button (only when non-empty); empty state copy: 'your searches will show up here.' in italic serif.
Recents are pushed only after a search that returned at least one song/album/playlist/userPlaylist (an artists-only match does NOT record); cap 10, newest-first, case-insensitive dedupe.
components.visualSpec: Two stacked sections, 28px gap (22px on mobile). Chips: pill buttons, 6px gap wrapping row, 12px sans font, 1px border at 45% ink, transparent bg; hover: 5% black bg + full-ink border. Headings: MonoLabel size 16, weight 500. Desktop >=1100px: 240px right rail, position:sticky top:24px. Mobile (<600px container): static, stacked below the results column.

components.name: DesktopSearch screen (headerless mobile variant)
components.purpose: The whole search surface: language pills, fetch orchestration, result sections, states.
behaviors: headerless=true on mobile: screen renders NO input and no intro labels — the MobileTopBar field is the input; only lang pills + results + sidebar render. Screen does not subscribe to the focus bus in this mode (top bar owns it).

Query: shared module store (searchQuery.js), debounced 300ms; fetch key = `${debouncedQ}|${lang}`; in-flight fetch aborted on key change; results written to a 12-entry module cache so back-navigation re-renders instantly with no refetch/flash.
Language pills: 'All' + 14 languages; selection persists in module scope (searchCache lastLang) across unmounts but not across reloads; changing pill refetches (lang param omitted for 'all').
langs param = onboarding seed languages (localStorage) — my-languages-first ranking server-side.
Section order: top hero (unless top is a song), then songs → artists → albums; if top is an album/movie: albums → songs → artists; then playlists, then your playlists. Sections hide when empty.
Family mode: dropExplicit() filters the songs section client-side (server PIN gate is the real boundary).
States: idle 'Your search results will appear here.' · loading AuraLoader 'Searching' · error 'Search failed — {msg}' · 'Nothing matched "q".'

Song tap -> onPickLive(track, element) plays it (with a morph origin element); tile taps route to artist/album/catalog-playlist/user-playlist screens setting return='search' so back lands on intact cached results.
Scroll memory per `search:{query}|{lang}` — restores scroll offset when returning from a detail screen; BackToTop floating button on long lists.
components.visualSpec: Container-query driven (container name dse). Header 40px/56px padding (14px/22px mobile). Mobile grid: 2 columns, 14px gap; desktop auto-fill minmax(190px,1fr), 18px gap. Song/entity tiles: square art radius 8 (round for artists), serif 18px title (15px mobile) single-line ellipsis, mono 9.5px artist/sub line. Fallback cover: first letter on accent gradient. Sections 44px apart (28px mobile), section titles sans 600 20px (22px mobile).

components.name: Top-result hero card
components.purpose: One best-match card that routes by entity type (artist/album/playlist pages); suppressed when the best match is a song (songs grid leads instead).
behaviors: Server sends `top` from the provider's autocomplete topquery; if it's an album, the server swaps in the language-ranked albums[0] (so a Kannada-first user gets Kannada 'KGF' as hero) and dedupes it out of the albums list.
Label under the name: 'Movie' vs 'Album' via isMovie, else capitalized type.
Tap routes: artist -> artist screen, album -> album detail, playlist -> catalog playlist detail.
components.visualSpec: Horizontal card, max-width 520px, 18px padding, radius 14, bg = ink@4% (8% hover), 92px square cover radius 10 (68px + 14px padding on mobile), serif 28px name (22px mobile), mono 10px type label. Artist hero cover is fully round.

components.name: Songs grid + per-song overflow (⋯)
components.purpose: Playable song results with a per-row actions menu.
behaviors: ⋯ button stops propagation and opens the GLOBAL track context menu at the button's rect (play / play next / add to queue / add to playlist / like / go to artist).
Rows also support right-click / long-press (500ms iOS timer) via the same bus elsewhere; on this screen only the ⋯ trigger is wired.
Second tap on the same ⋯ toggles the menu closed.
components.visualSpec: 40px round dark chip (black@45%, white glyph) pinned top-right over the art. Desktop: opacity 0, revealed on tile hover. (hover:none) or <900px: always visible — the web already solved the no-hover case; native should just always show it or move actions to long-press.

components.name: MobileTopBar morph-to-search field
components.purpose: Mobile search entry + the actual input while searching (screen is input-less).
behaviors: Brand area AND a magnifier button both open search; the pill cross-fades (transform+opacity only) between bar-content and searchfield layers; inactive layer gets `inert`.

stateAndStorage: Query text: module-scope singleton (src/lib/searchQuery.js) shared between MobileTopBar input and the screen; survives screen unmount; NOT persisted; cleared on search close.
Results cache: module-scope Map (src/lib/searchCache.js), key `query|lang`, max 12 entries, freshest-last eviction; makes back-navigation instant; in-memory only.
Language pill: module-scope lastLang in searchCache.js — survives unmount, resets on reload (default 'all').
Recent searches: localStorage 'aura.recentSearches', JSON string array, cap 10, newest-first, case-insensitive dedupe; only written after a result-bearing search; clear() empties it.
User language priority (the `langs` param): localStorage via getSeedSignals() from onboarding (src/lib/onboarding.js).
Scroll position: useScrollMemory keyed `search:{query}|{lang}`, restored when status==='ok' (cached results give correct height immediately).
Focus intent: searchFocus.js bus with a buffered `pending` flag (fires post-mount).

Server-side: suggest LRU (80 entries, per lowered query) in server/catalog.js; cacheTracks(songs) fire-and-forget after each search response (feeds the tracks table so playlists/likes can reference them).
Auth state: web = httpOnly cookie aura_session (SameSite=Strict, 30d); a 401 triggers client revalidateSession().
portingNotes: TRENDING IS NOT AN ENDPOINT. It is a hardcoded 6-strings-per-language map in SearchSidebar.jsx with no refresh cadence (deploy-time only) — per the 'neat system, no tricks' rule, the native app should either ship the same static list knowingly, or skip trending; there is no server trending route to call. The only server-side trending data (upstream new_trending via getCatalogHome) feeds the discover/featured pool internally and is not exposed. If server-driven trending is wanted, that's a new endpoint to build, not one to find.

Native app search currently lacks (vs web mobile): trending chips per language, top-result hero card with entity routing, catalog Playlists group, 'Your playlists' group (userPlaylists, signed-in), albums-first section reordering when the top result is an album/movie, Movie badge + 'Movie/Album · year' subtitles, per-song overflow menu (play next / add to queue / add to playlist / like / go to artist), Family-mode explicit filtering of the songs section, `langs` my-languages-first ranking param, 12-entry result cache + per-query scroll restoration on back-nav, recents-only-on-successful-results rule, the four distinct idle/loading/error/nothing states, and BackToTop.
Send limit=12 and langs=<priority-ordered user languages> like the web client does — the server's album hero promotion and language ranking only activate with langs; omit lang for the 'All' pill.

Auth for the same live API: login with header X-Aura-Client: native — the server then returns the session JWT in the response body (server/auth.js:61); send it back as Authorization: Bearer <token> (middleware/auth.js accepts Bearer as a first-class fallback; peekUserId checks header then cookie). Without auth, /api/catalog/search still works but userPlaylists is always [].

Hover-only UI needs rethink: the per-song ⋯ chip is opacity-0 until tile :hover on desktop; web already forces it visible under (hover:none)/<900px — native should always render it (or move actions to long-press, which the web's context-menu bus also supports with a 500ms timer on iOS). The translateY(-1px) tile hover lift and input :focus-within accent underline have no native equivalent — drop or replace with pressed-state feedback.

Layout is CSS-container-query driven (@container dse max-width:600px -> 2-col grid, 22px gutters) and the sidebar is position:sticky on desktop but stacks BELOW results on mobile. For native, per the 'reimagine mobile' rule: recents + trending belong as the PRE-QUERY body content (native already shows recents there), not appended under results.

The whole morph-to-search apparatus (inert layers, synchronous focus-in-gesture for iOS keyboard, capture-phase pointerdown tracking + setTimeout(0) races for blur-collapse, the buffered focus bus) exists to fight browser keyboard/focus semantics — RN gets all of this for free with TextInput focus()/Keyboard APIs; do not port it.

Debounce is 300ms with AbortController cancellation of stale requests; recreate with a timer + fetch cancellation. The `${query}|${lang}` cache key discipline (render from cache when present, skip fetch) is what makes back-navigation flash-free — worth porting as-is (MMKV or in-memory Map).

songs[].streamUrl in the search response is a fully decrypted, directly playable CDN .mp4 URL at the configured bitrate — feed it straight to ExoPlayer/RNTP. Note cold-start caveat from the queue system: stored stream URLs go stale (CDN tokens), so refetch via GET /api/catalog/track/:id when resuming old items.

imageUrl/image fields are already bumped to the large CDN size server-side (bumpImg/pickImageUrl); artist images are square files rendered round by CSS border-radius — apply borderRadius natively. Fallback cover (no image) = first letter of the name on an accent gradient tile, replicate in native.

localStorage recents ('aura.recentSearches', cap 10, case-insensitive dedupe, push only when the response had songs/albums/playlists/userPlaylists) -> MMKV with identical semantics so behavior matches web.

Web-only, skip entirely: '/' keyboard shortcut -> focus bus, webkit search-input clear-button suppression CSS, prefers-reduced-motion guards on the 460ms/320ms open/close screen animations (use native transitions), and the onClose X button (hidden on mobile web anyway — bottom nav owns back).

portingNotes: Auth: web sends the httpOnly session-cookie JWT via plain fetch (fetchAuthed adds nothing — it only triggers revalidateSession on 401). The native app cannot read that cookie; the server already accepts `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` as a fallback (D:\Brave Downloads\AI Music Development\server\middleware\auth.js lines 77-82, covered by auth.native-token.test.js) — use that path.

Hover-only affordances to rethink: (1) the per-row 3-dot overflow button is opacity:0 and only revealed on row :hover (DesktopLibrary.css lines 361-377) — invisible-but-tappable on touch today; native should make it always visible, or use long-press/swipe → action sheet. (2) Closed shelves 'crack open' on hover (@media(hover) padding-bottom grow + peek shift, lines 270-283) — desktop-only preview, drop it.

The accordion animation is a pure-CSS trick: grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr with a delayed visibility:hidden on a clip layer to keep collapsed content out of the a11y tree/tab order. Native needs Reanimated/LayoutAnimation height animation and simply not rendering (or setting accessibilityElementsHidden on) collapsed content.

Track context menu (toggleTrackMenu) is positioned at DOM getBoundingClientRect coordinates (x:right, y:bottom of the trigger) — replace with a bottom sheet / ActionSheet on native; DesktopLiked passes menu:{omit:['like']} to avoid duplicating the heart action, keep that option concept.

State persistence is web-storage based: open shelf in sessionStorage 'aura.libraryShelf' (intentionally session-scoped — fresh visits land all-closed), scroll offsets via useScrollMemory (per-key store fed by a passive scroll listener, restored pre-paint), tap hints in localStorage 'aura.hint.<id>' (max 3 shows, killed on first real interaction). Port to MMKV / navigation state; preserve the session-vs-permanent distinction.

Navigation is screen-state strings (setScreen('library'|'liked'|'history'|'playlists'|'playlist-detail')) with explicit return-screen props (onClose → setScreen('library')) — no URL router. Native gets a real navigator; map the return-screen contract onto the nav stack.

History list semantics matter for FlatList: rows are one-per-play (duplicates of the same track are expected), keyed `${id}-${playedAt}`; pagination is an explicit 'Load more' button on the web — native can use onEndReached but must keep the `before` cursor (unix-ms) protocol and nextBefore:null as the stop signal.

Music clock is computed client-side in LOCAL time (server returns UTC ms; summarizeClock buckets by device-local hour) — same logic ports directly; keep it client-side so 'your 2am songs' stay correct per device timezone.
Day-group headings and play times in History use device-locale APIs (toLocaleDateString weekday/month/day, 12-hour formatTime12) — use the RN i18n equivalents.

Likes are an app-lifetime module singleton with optimistic writes and rollback; the `ready` guard exists because filtering a server list through a not-yet-booted like set rendered Liked as empty — reproduce both the optimism and the ready gate in the native store (zustand/MMKV), and keep the fire-toast-before-network UX.

Like/unlike also invalidates the client-side home quickPicks cache (invalidateHomeCache('quickPicks') in src/api/likes.js) — replicate that cross-surface invalidation or quick picks go stale after liking.

PlaylistsScreen consumes ?join=TOKEN from window.location and strips it with history.replaceState — native needs a deep-link/App Link route that feeds the token to acceptPlaylistInvite with the same strip-before-accept idempotency.
tzOffset convention: /api/playlists/auto (and history clock precedent) expect JS getTimezoneOffset() semantics (minutes, inverted sign vs UTC offset) — send the same convention from native.

Web images use loading='lazy' with letter-fallback spans for missing covers; the peek 'fan' overlaps three 26px covers with negative margins — trivial in RN but it's custom layout, not a library component.

Auto-mix cards embed their full track list in the list response (a.tracks) so ▶ plays without a detail fetch — keep consuming that; the inline play control is a nested role='button' span inside the card button (nested-interactive hack for web a11y), which native should model as two separate touchables.

Route-order dependency on the shared API: /api/playlists/auto and /api/playlists/saved are matched before /api/playlists/:id — nothing to port, but never request /api/playlists/auto expecting a playlist named 'auto'.

Server response quirk: /api/likes track rows come from a LEFT JOIN on the tracks cache — a liked track missing from `tracks` yields a row with null title/artist/streamUrl (id from l.track_id is also null in rowToTrack since it reads t.id); native list rendering must tolerate null fields.
Copy voice: all empty states are plain and lowercase-leaning ('nothing yet', 'No liked songs yet. Tap the heart on any track.') — keep exact strings per the plain-copy-voice memory rule.
stateAndStorage: sessionStorage 'aura.libraryShelf' — which accordion shelf is open (null = all closed); cleared when the open shelf is toggled shut

components.name: Edition system (server/autoPlaylists.js + tasteScore.js + mix_editions)
components.purpose: An 'edition' = a dated, immutable-membership snapshot of one mix for one user, keyed by the USER'S local calendar date and cached forever in mix_editions (the archive)
behaviors: Edition keys: on-repeat/morning/night → localDateKey (today, 'YYYY-MM-DD'); new-to-you → lastFridayKey; bring-it-back → lastMondayKey — key advances at the local boundary, generating the next edition on first read past it

Payload stored as {tracks:[{trackId, reason}], meta:{tz,...}, description?} — trackIds only; serve-time hydration re-JOINs tracks so metadata/streamUrls stay fresh, suppressed tracks drop out immediately, vanished tracks skip

new-to-you fallback: if the fresh build is thin/errors, the previous edition is served with refreshing:true and ITS edition_key (honest dating); nightly cron retries

Generators: on-repeat = top 28d-half-life scores, >=2 plays, cap 2/artist, top 30; bring-it-back = 180d-half-life score, dormant >=60d, >=3 plays, top 25, month-of-last-play receipts; morning/night = 28d scores restricted to local daypart (05-10:59 / 20:00-03:59), >=40 daypart plays across kept tracks else omitted, top 20; all mixes omitted under 5 tracks
Suppression (skip-shelved: >=2 skips in 90d + never finished + not liked; plus explicitly hidden) excluded at generation AND serve time
editionLabel formatted server-side: 'edition · ' + lowercase 'ddd D mmm' from the UTC parse of the key

stateAndStorage: Server: mix_editions table (migration v22) — PK (user_id, mix_key, edition_key), payload JSONB {tracks:[{trackId,reason}], meta:{tz, langShares?, seedIds?, carriedOver?}, description?}, generated_at BIGINT ms; rows are NEVER deleted (past editions are the archive); index idx_mix_editions_latest (user_id, mix_key, generated_at DESC) backs 'latest edition' fallback reads

Server: track_similarity graph (written by auto-radio) + live getRelatedTracks stations feed new-to-you candidates; chosen station tracks are persisted via cacheTracks before storing the edition
Client: homeCache module object (in-memory, session-lifetime, no persistence) with key 'autoPlaylists'; SWR refresh on every Home mount; invalidated on hide
Client: the open mix's descriptor lives in React state (App.autoPlaylist via setAutoPlaylist) — passed by reference from the shelf to the detail screen; no URL param, no deep link, lost on reload
Client: tzOffset sent on every list call as new Date().getTimezoneOffset() — the server clamps and stores it in payload.meta.tz, and the nightly cron reuses that stored tz per user
portingNotes: No per-mix endpoint exists: the detail view is fed in-memory from the single GET /api/playlists/auto response. A native detail screen restored after process death (or deep-linked) must refetch the whole list and find the mix by mixKey — or persist the last descriptor locally.

Always send tzOffset (JS getTimezoneOffset convention: minutes to ADD to local to get UTC, IST = -330). Omitting it keys editions to UTC and the user's 'daily' boundary shifts. RN's Date#getTimezoneOffset matches the web value.

Auth for the same live API: web rides the httpOnly aura_session cookie; native must send X-Aura-Client: native at login to receive the JWT in the response body, then Authorization: Bearer <jwt> on every call (server middleware accepts either).

Hover-revealed play chip is web-only CSS (.aura-dh__playlist-play opacity 0 → 1 on :hover/:focus-within, force-shown via container query on touch). Native: make the play affordance always visible, as the phone breakpoint already does.

DesktopHome is ONE component serving desktop and phone via CSS container queries (both QuickPicks variants render, one display:none'd). Do not port this pattern — build the native mix shelf as its own purposeful layout (per the 'reimagine mobile' discipline).

Playing a mix: no play endpoint — the client sets its queue to the descriptor's prebuilt tracks array (streamUrl on every row) and starts at index N. pickLiveSequence also runs a morphInto FLIP animation from the tapped DOM element to the player — replace with a native shared-element transition or drop it.

Daypart windowing of morning/night mixes on Home is CLIENT-side (new Date().getHours(): morning 5-11, night >=20 or <4) — replicate in the native home; the playlists surface always shows the full suite with the DAYPART_NOTE captions.
Treat editionKey/editionLabel/cadence/refreshing/ruleLine/reason as opaque server display strings — do not recompute or re-derive them client-side; the server owns the honesty contract.

Caching contract to replicate: render cached mixes instantly, refetch on every screen focus (stale-while-revalidate) — membership/order legitimately change mid-session (on-repeat rekey after 15 plays, weekly mixes reorder at local midnight, edition boundaries at local day / Mon / Fri). A cache older than the local day is stale by design.
After POST /api/hidden the app must drop any cached mixes AND quick picks (web does invalidateHomeCache('autoPlaylists','quickPicks')) and optimistically remove the row from the open detail.
Gate cards (kind 'auto-gate', only ever new-to-you) are informational and non-interactive — render gate.line, no navigation, no play.
Mixes thinner than 5 tracks are omitted server-side, so the suite length varies 0-5; the shelf must self-hide when empty (web does).

Mix covers are just the first track's imageUrl (coverImageUrl, nullable) — the fallback is a ♫ tile, and per-track art fallback is a CSS-procedural pattern (rings/bands/circle/split/noise monogram + vignette, CSS color-mix + theme vars). Native needs these redrawn (e.g. Skia/SVG) or a simpler monogram fallback.

Web-only bits that don't port: loading='lazy'/decoding='async' imgs, :hover translateY lift on cards, focus-within, JSON-LD/tab-title meta, useScrollMemory keyed DOM scroll restoration, AbortController-per-mount fetch cancellation (map to your fetch layer).

Edition pre-warm is infra: Vercel Cron hits GET /api/lyrics-jobs/process (Bearer CRON_SECRET) daily 02:00 UTC ≈ 07:30 IST so the morning open finds today's editions; cold cache misses still generate inline on read (the list call can take a few seconds first-open of a new local day — show a skeleton).
The '{Mode} mix' card at the top of Home is a DIFFERENT feature (mode-pool play-all, not an edition) — don't conflate it with the made-for-you suite.
There is no pull-to-refresh/manual refresh endpoint for mixes: freshness is entirely read-triggered; re-calling GET /api/playlists/auto is the refresh.
Track reasons ('receipts') are per-edition and can reference counts that have since changed — that's intentional (the edition is a dated snapshot); show them verbatim under the title as the web does.

URL sync (lib/routes.js + usePathRoute): /artist/:id, /artist/by-name/:name, /album/:id, /catalog/:id, /lang/:lang are shareable deep links; auto mixes and shared playlists render from in-memory objects with NO URL (refresh → home). searchCache: results cached per 'query|lang' key so returning from an entity screen re-renders instantly without refetch; recent searches persisted (pushRecentSearch); search language filter persisted (getSearchLang/setSearchLang).

scrollMemory: per-key scroll offsets (artist:<k>, album:<id>, catalog:<id>, lang:<lang>, search:<q|lang>) restored pre-paint via useLayoutEffect once data is ready — native gets this from list state preservation.

Server-side caches the native app inherits for free: artist LRU(100), album LRU(100), suggest LRU(80) per instance; discover home cached per language per UTC day (shelf queries embed current month/year).

Auth: web rides the httpOnly aura_session cookie via fetchAuthed (no header). Server middleware ALSO accepts Authorization: Bearer <jwt>, and login with header X-Aura-Client: native returns the JWT in the response body — this is the native app's path. /api/artists/lookup, /api/albums/:id, /api/discover/* need no auth; /api/catalog/search is optionalAuth (auth adds userPlaylists bucket); /api/playlists/auto and /api/hidden require auth.
portingNotes: Hover-revealed controls everywhere: the row ⋯ button is opacity ~0 until .aura-dpd__row:hover; home/hub tile play overlays appear on :hover (touch media query already forces opacity:1 as a fallback). Native: make the ⋯ always visible or use swipe actions/long-press — do not hide affordances.

TrackContextMenu is a floating popup at pointer coordinates with desktop right-click + a hand-rolled 500ms iOS long-press shim (ctxPress) and keyboard navigation. Native rethink: a standard bottom sheet triggered by ⋯ tap and row long-press; keep the omit/extras tailoring model (artist screen omits 'open artist'; auto mixes add 'don't show this again').

Play handlers take an optional srcEl (e.currentTarget) to run a shared-element morph of the tapped artwork into the player art (morphInto, ~470ms). Native should use its own transition system; the srcEl param is web-only and ignorable.

None of the four screens has a shuffle button — only 'Play all' / 'Play top tracks'. Shuffle is a queue/player-screen concern: ON shuffles only the up-next tail (current track + history pinned), OFF just clears the indicator without restoring order. Replicate exactly or intentionally diverge.

streamUrl in every Track is a decrypted upstream CDN URL that can expire. Web refreshes lazily via GET /api/catalog/track/:id when a stale track becomes current (persisted queue path). The native queue (ExoPlayer) must implement the same on-demand refresh, ideally on playback-error retry too.

responses are inconsistently wrapped — mind the shapes: /api/artists/lookup → {artist}, /api/albums/:id → {album}, but /api/discover/home, /api/discover/playlist/:id and /api/catalog/track/:id return the object UNWRAPPED; /api/catalog/search returns the buckets at top level.

Artist can be opened by NAME only (home top-artists rail sends {name, trackId}; context menu likewise) — server-side resolution can 404 ('no catalog artist match'); the screen shows an inline error with a working back. Prefer passing trackId whenever a track is at hand — it's the deterministic path.

album.artist is a comma-joined string of every contributor; the web screen shows only split(',')[0]. topArtists rail items have NO catalog artist id (artist is a play-history name string), so artist ids must never be assumed present.

Explicit filtering is uneven by design: search songs are filtered client-side under explicit-off modes (dropExplicit), but artist top tracks, album tracklists, and catalog playlist tracks are NOT filtered on these screens (the queue prunes explicit tracks on mode switch). Decide native policy consciously.

No pagination anywhere on these surfaces — fixed caps (artist: 15 tracks/12 albums fetched, 10/8 shown; hub shelves: 12 fetched, 8 shown; search limit 12 on web, ≤40 max). Native can render the full fetched arrays; there is no 'load more' API.

Auto mixes and shared playlists have NO per-id GET — the list endpoint returns full track arrays and the detail screen renders from memory (initialData). Native must pass the whole object through navigation (or re-fetch the list), and auto-mix ids/editions change over time so don't persist them as routes.
Track rows / tiles use CSS hover lift (translateY(-1px)) and focus-visible rings — purely decorative; replace with native press states.

Screen enter animations (ScreenTransition), Suspense chunk skeletons with label-matched loaders (skeleton label = the screen's own loading label, e.g. 'Loading Tamil'), and BackToTop floating button are web chrome; per-screen document titles + JSON-LD (setMeta) are web/SEO-only — skip in native.

cleanTitle() is applied to every displayed track title and artist/album names render lowercased via CSS/JS (brand style); reuse the same utils (src/utils/title.js, src/utils/fmtTime.js fmtTime/fmtRuntime) for visual parity.

Web-only per-fetch AbortController on every screen (cancel on unmount/param change) — mirror with request cancellation in the native client to avoid stale-response races when tapping through artists quickly.

Search screen caches results per query|lang and restores scroll so back-from-album is instant; without an equivalent native cache, back navigation will refetch and lose position — the /api/catalog/search response is small (limit 12), so an in-memory LRU keyed the same way suffices.

Batching: one POST per surface render carrying the whole shown list (max 40) — there is no queue/flush timer; the 'batch' is the single array. Server writes all rows in ONE multi-VALUES INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id,track_id,surface,day) DO UPDATE count=count+1, last_ts=now (query retries=0)

Only call site today: DesktopHome quick-picks shelf — logs the 8 shown ids as surface 'quick-picks' ONLY when the server ring supplied >=4 tracks (the local most-played/recent/featured fallback is never logged since it isn't the demotable surface)
Day bucketing: server computes user-local day via clampTzOffset(tzOffset) + localDateKey; count climbs per session that re-showed, but DISTINCT-day count drives demotion so double-logs are harmless

Read path (getImpressionSignals per surface): unplayedShownDays = distinct days shown with NO 'play' listening_event since first shown -> score multiplied by 0.85^days (applyPenalty); cooldown = shown >=3 distinct days unplayed AND last shown within 7 days -> held out of rotation slots entirely. Anchors (top-3, demonstrably played) are exempt. Signal-read failure degrades to 'no demotion', never a broken response
Also feeds the 'something new' exploration slot: candidates ordered by least total shown count (SUM(count) for surface 'quick-picks') so it self-corrects
Retention: rows with last_ts older than 90 days pruned by the daily cron (best-effort, piggybacked on /api/lyrics-jobs/process)

components.name: DesktopQueue drag-reorder
components.purpose: Reorder the live queue by dragging rows; one component serves desktop and phone (container queries switch chrome at <=600px)
behaviors: Two pickup modes: mouse = instant drag from the 6-dot grab handle (pointerdown -> beginDrag with setPointerCapture); touch = 450ms long-press anywhere on the row body (haptic tap(12) on arm; >10px movement before the timer = scroll, cancels; draggedRef suppresses the row's click-to-play right after a drag)

Geometry: at drag start it snapshots getBoundingClientRect (top/height) of every visible [data-row], each tagged with its ABSOLUTE track index from data-idx (collapsed 'past' rows are excluded via :not(.aura-dq__past-wrap--collapsed [data-row]) so zero-height phantoms don't skew drops); hover target = first row whose midpoint is below effectiveY (pointerY + scrollDelta since drag start)
Edge auto-scroll: within 90px of the scroller's top/bottom, rAF loop scrolls at up to 16px/frame proportional to edge proximity, recomputing hoverTo as it scrolls

Visuals: dragged row translateY(pointer delta + scrollDelta) scale(1.01) zIndex 5; other rows shift +-one row height with 240ms cubic-bezier(.25,.85,.3,1) transform transition; while dragging, document-level non-passive touchmove preventDefault blocks page scroll (React's onTouchMove is passive so it wouldn't take)

Drop: onDragEnd calls onReorder(from, hoverTo) only if indices differ. App.jsx reorderQueue is pure array math: splice out, splice in, then fix currentIdx (from===idx -> idx=to; from<idx<=to -> idx-1; to<=idx<from -> idx+1). Bounds-checked no-op otherwise
No endpoint — queue order is client state only, persisted locally via lib/persistentQueue.js (localStorage 'aura.queue'); nothing is synced to the server on reorder

Adjacent queue actions: x removes any non-current row (removeFromQueue fixes idx), 'Hide past' collapses played rows (localStorage 'aura.queueHidePast', grid 0fr animation, rows stay in DOM), shuffle = client Fisher-Yates of tracks[idx+1..] with sticky indicator (turning off does NOT restore order), repeat cycles off/all/one, clear keeps only the playing track after a confirm, overflow menu: save as playlist / add all to a playlist / clear; on-mount scroll centers (<=600px) or near-tops the now-playing row

Auto-next: sitting on the last non-wrapping track shows the prefetched continuation batch (from GET /api/tracks/:id/related) as a faded 'Up next · Picked by AURA' list; clicking fills the batch into the queue and plays from that row; hidden in repeat modes and for "tonight's set"
components.visualSpec: Rows: handle (6-dot SVG) | 2-digit index | 54px art | title/artist | duration | '...' | x. Dragged row lifts with scale(1.01); collapse animation via grid-template-rows 0fr wrapper

components.name: Sleep timer (lib singleton + sheet + orb)
components.purpose: Pause playback after a chosen duration or when the current set finishes
behaviors: Options (SleepTimerSheet PRESETS): 10 / 20 / 30 / 45 / 60 minutes, plus 'end of set' sentinel, plus 'cancel timer' when armed. Arming toasts 'sleep in N min.' / 'sleep at end of set.'; cancel toasts 'sleep timer cancelled.' Sheet shows a live M:SS countdown (Math.ceil so it never shows 0:00 early) or 'end of set' while armed; re-arming replaces the previous timer (start() calls cancel() first)

Mechanics: endsAt timestamp + 1s setInterval poll instead of setTimeout — background tabs throttle timers, so wall-clock comparison keeps it accurate after backgrounding. State pushed to subscribers every tick. Deliberately NOT persisted — reload/app restart disarms

Fire (duration): interval sees Date.now() >= endsAt -> cancel() then fireExpiry('duration') -> App.jsx subscribeSleepFire handler does setPlaying(false) + toast 'sleep timer · paused.' No fade-out — a hard pause; the current track position is retained (normal pause semantics)

Fire (end-of-set): start('end-of-set') only sets a flag (no countdown). In the player's ended handler (App.jsx:868), when the queue cannot advance — the exact moment it would otherwise wrap ("tonight's set"/repeat-all) or fall through to auto-radio — fireEndOfSetIfArmed() clears the flag, pauses, sets ended, toasts 'set ended · sleeping.' It preempts both wrap-around and the auto-radio continuation

Entry points: SpeedDial action (App.jsx:2019), DesktopRail mini action (DesktopRail.jsx:169), MobilePlayer overflow menu (MobilePlayer.jsx:91), and clicking the orb. Sheet is a focus-trapped dialog (Tab wraps, Escape closes, focus restored to opener)

SleepTimerOrb: floating 52px button visible whenever armed and the sheet is closed; SVG progress ring (dasharray = remaining/total, glow head dot rides the arc), label = M:SS or 'end of set', urgent styling at <=60s; draggable via pointer capture with 5px click-vs-drag threshold — release without movement opens the sheet; position stored as right/bottom insets in localStorage 'aura.sleepOrbPos', clamped on resize, offset by 420px when the desktop rail is open (CSS transition eases the slide); default resting spot bottom 88px desktop / 128px mobile (clears the dock)
Entirely client-side: no API endpoint involved anywhere in the sleep timer
components.visualSpec: Orb: crescent-moon icon + 3 twinkle stars, circular countdown ring r=23 in a 52px disc, mono countdown label, 6-dot grip; sheet: dark modal with preset buttons list + breathing accent dot beside the live countdown

Auth/session: httpOnly cookie on web (fetchAuthed attaches nothing; 401 triggers session revalidation); server also accepts Authorization: Bearer <same JWT> — native clients get the token in the login response body by sending X-Aura-Client: native
portingNotes: Auth for native: do NOT try to read the web cookie. Send X-Aura-Client: native on login/verify — server then includes the JWT as body.token (server/auth.js:54-62); thereafter send Authorization: Bearer <token> (accepted by requireAuth cookie-first-then-bearer, server/middleware/auth.js:77-82). Store in MMKV. fetchAuthed uses relative paths — native needs the absolute base (aurafm.live).

Context menu trigger is deeply web-shaped: onContextMenu (right-click), a hand-rolled 500ms iOS touch long-press with Android contextmenu double-open suppression, plus DOM-only close behaviors (outside mousedown, capture-phase scroll close, window blur, Escape/Tab, roving menuitem focus) and a data-track-menu-trigger attribute hack for '...' toggle. Native rethink: RN long-press gesture -> bottom-sheet action list. KEEP the data model as-is — base action ids ['play','playNext','addToQueue','addToPlaylist','like'/'unlike','artist'] with per-surface omit[] and extras[] ({label, onClick, danger}) ports cleanly.

Play / play-next / add-to-queue / reorder / shuffle / clear / remove are ALL client-side queue mutations — no queue API exists. The native app must own its ExoPlayer queue and reproduce App.jsx's index math (enqueueNext splices at idx+1 and flips source "tonight's set"->'your set' to kill wrap-around; reorderQueue/removeFromQueue idx fixups at App.jsx:1276-1304). Queue persistence is localStorage-only on web — native should persist its own queue (MMKV) rather than expect server sync.

Hide: no inline undo window anywhere — the toast just points to Settings. Native needs the Settings 'hidden songs' list (GET /api/hidden / DELETE /api/hidden/:id) for parity, and must replicate the client-side cache invalidation of mixes + quick picks after hide/unhide, or the freshly-hidden track will keep appearing until the next cold fetch. Hide is only offered on tracks whose containing list has kind==='auto' (made-for-you mixes).

Impressions: only log the server-served quick-picks ring (>=4 served), exactly the ids actually rendered (8), surface string 'quick-picks', cap 40, fire-and-forget with the once-per-(surface, day)-per-app-session guard; release the guard on network failure so a later screen visit retries. Note a quirk to decide on: the client guard key uses the UTC date (toISOString) while the server buckets by tzOffset-local day — mirror the web behavior or key the guard by local day; either is safe because server dedupes by distinct-day.

Impression semantics for a native scrolling UI: web logs on render of the shelf (once/day), NOT per-item viewport visibility. Don't over-engineer per-item view tracking — matching web behavior keeps server signals comparable.

Queue drag-reorder is 100% web DOM (PointerEvents + setPointerCapture, getBoundingClientRect snapshots keyed by data-idx, rAF edge auto-scroll at 90px/16px-per-frame, non-passive document touchmove preventDefault, CSS transform shifts). Rebuild with a native draggable list (e.g. react-native-draggable-flatlist over RNGH + Reanimated) and call the same pure reorder(from, to) reducer. Web's touch pickup = 450ms long-press with 10px slop and a haptic tap(12) — match that feel; suppress row-press->play immediately after a drag (web uses draggedRef for this exact race).

'Hide past' in the queue is a purely visual collapse persisted in localStorage — trivial to port as a local preference; remember drag-drop index math must skip collapsed rows (web excludes them from the rect snapshot).

Sleep timer is entirely client-side (zero endpoints) and intentionally non-persistent across restarts. The web's 1s-interval-vs-setTimeout choice exists ONLY because of browser background-tab throttling — in the native app, implement at the audio-service layer (ExoPlayer/RNTP: pause at deadline, or 'end of set' = pause instead of advancing when the queue's last track completes BEFORE wrap/auto-radio kicks in). The end-of-set trigger point matters: it preempts repeat-all wrap AND the auto-radio continuation (App.jsx:868).

SleepTimerOrb (draggable floating chip with localStorage position, desktop-rail offset, CSS transition) is web chrome — replace with a countdown chip in the player UI + the media notification; keep the <=60s urgent state and M:SS ceil formatting for parity.

Family/explicit filtering of quick picks happens CLIENT-side (dropExplicit over the 12 served, show 8) using the per-track explicit flag — the native client must apply the same filter, and the daypart label ('your evening picks') mirrors server boundaries 5/12/17/21 local hours.

Toasts are load-bearing UX confirmations throughout ('queued next.', 'hidden — ... undo in settings.', 'sleep timer · paused.') — plain lowercase copy voice; reuse the exact strings for product-voice consistency.

Hover-only affordances to rethink: desktop rows reveal '...' / x / grab-handle on CSS hover; on native every row needs always-visible or swipe-revealed actions. The web's row long-press is already claimed by the context menu on most surfaces but by drag-pickup in the queue — that per-surface long-press meaning collision needs an explicit native decision (e.g. queue: long-press = drag, '...' = menu).

endpoints.purpose: The featured pool that drives THREE home sections: hero band = tracks[0], 'New for you' = tracks[1..4], 'Stations' = tracks[5..8]. App fetches it (useFeaturedTracks, limit 24) and passes it to DesktopHome as `tracks`; mode-seeded server-side from the auth'd user's active mode (everyday = global default). Refetched on every mode switch.
endpoints.params: Query: limit (number, client sends 24), lang (optional). Auth optional (cookie session); signed-in users get their active mode's seeded pool.
endpoints.responseShape: { results: Track[] } where Track = { id, title, artist, album, language, durationSec, streamUrl, imageUrl, explicit: boolean } (server/catalog.js mapSong). Client applies dropExplicit when family mode is on.

endpoints.purpose: Server-ranked Quick Picks ring: top-3 frecency 'anchors' + rotating slots re-seeded per user-local daypart + one 'something new' exploration pick from the user's similarity graph. Each pick carries a plain-sentence `reason`. Cached in homeCache for the session; refetched with `salt` on the shuffle-all action (desktop orbit only).
endpoints.params: Query: tzOffset (REQUIRED by client — new Date().getTimezoneOffset(), minutes, JS sign convention; keys the daily edition + daypart to the user's local day), salt (optional, ≤32 chars, rerolls rotating slots only). Auth required.
endpoints.responseShape: { tracks: [{ ...Track, explicit, reason: string (e.g. 'you finished this 3× lately' | 'you liked this' | '5 plays this month' | 'you played this recently' | 'something new'), anchor: boolean, exploration?: true }], editionKey: 'YYYY-MM-DD', cadence: 'rotates daily', daypart: 'morning'|'afternoon'|'evening'|'night' }. Up to 12 tracks (client shows 8 after family filter); sparse histories topped up from recently-played; can return fewer than 4 → client falls back to local derivation.

endpoints.purpose: Logs which quick picks were actually SHOWN so the ranker can demote shown-but-never-played picks. Fired once per (surface='quick-picks', local day) per SPA session, ONLY when the server ring (≥4 picks) is what rendered — the local fallback is never logged. Fire-and-forget; failure releases the guard for retry.
endpoints.params: JSON body: { surface: 'quick-picks', tzOffset: number, track_ids: string[] (client caps at 40) }. Auth required.
endpoints.responseShape: 200 empty-ish ack; 400 { error: 'invalid surface or track_ids' }.

endpoints.purpose: Quick-picks fallback tier 1 (used when the server ring has <4 picks) and the 'About you' DNA card's track count. Not directly a visible shelf on home.
endpoints.params: Query: days (default 30), limit (default 10; client sends defaults). Auth required.
endpoints.responseShape: { tracks: [{ ...Track, playCount: number }] } — 30-day play-count ranking.

endpoints.purpose: 'Your top artists' rail (up to 8 round avatar tiles) + feeds the 'About you' DNA card headline and the section's visibility.
endpoints.responseShape: { artists: [{ artist: string, playCount: number, sampleTrack: Track }] } — sampleTrack is the artist's most-played track; its imageUrl becomes the avatar.

endpoints.purpose: 'Recently played' memory-tile rail (home shows first 3) + quick-picks fallback tier 2.
endpoints.responseShape: { tracks: Track[] } — deduped one row per track, newest first.

endpoints.purpose: 'Your playlists' grid (home shows first 4). Includes playlists the user collaborates on.
endpoints.responseShape: { playlists: [{ id, name, description, trackCount, coverImageUrl (custom upload wins over cover-track art, else null), updatedAt (ms), role: 'owner'|'editor'|'viewer', shared: boolean }] }

endpoints.purpose: 'Made for you' mixes (on repeat / new to you / bring it back / your morning songs / your night songs). Each mix ships its FULL playable track list so the ▶ chip plays without a detail fetch. The ONE home fetch that is stale-while-revalidate: cached copy renders instantly, a fresh fetch runs on EVERY mount and updates in place.
endpoints.params: Query: tzOffset (getTimezoneOffset(), keys editions + daily reorder to the user's calendar day). Auth required. NOTE: route must stay matched before /api/playlists/:id.
endpoints.responseShape: { playlists: [{ id: 'auto:<mixKey>', kind: 'auto' | 'auto-gate', mixKey: 'on-repeat'|'new-to-you'|'bring-it-back'|'morning'|'night', name, description, tracks: [{ ...Track, reason }] (empty for gates), trackCount, coverImageUrl (first track's art, else null), ruleLine, editionKey?, editionLabel?, cadence?: 'updates daily'|'new every friday'|'new every monday', refreshing?: boolean, gate?: { need, have, line: "unlocks after ~N songs — you're at X" } }] }. ## (1) Scope items missing or thinly mapped

- **Mode switching machinery (under the "mode mix card" scope item) — the one real gap.** The map documents the card and says "switchMode → refetches the featured pool" but never maps the endpoint or data model:
  - `POST /api/modes/active` (`server/modesRoutes.js`, requireAuth, body `{key}`, 400 `{error:'unknown mode', code:'bad_mode'}`, returns `{user: sanitizeUser(...)}`) is the only way to switch modes. The featured pool is seeded server-side from `users.active_mode` (`server/app.js:257-277`), so an RN port cannot drive the "curating your {mode} mix…" flow at all without this route. It's behind the `sensitiveLimiter` (`app.js:126`).
  - The modes catalog, `activeMode`, and per-mode `explicitOff` all ride on the auth user object (`App.jsx:342-350`: `user?.activeMode`, `user?.modes`, `explicitOff = modes.find(activeMode)?.explicitOff ?? user?.familyMode`). The map invokes "family mode on" for `dropExplicit` in four areas but never says where the flag comes from.
  - `App.jsx:366-379`: effect that prunes explicit tracks from the live queue when switching into an explicit-off mode — mentioned in one porting note as a side comment, mechanics unmapped.
- **`POST /api/events` (listening recorder, `app.js:1005`) — thinly referenced.** Every Phase-2 personalization surface (quick-picks frecency, editions, top artists, recently played, history, impressions' "played since" demotion, skip-shelving) derives from `listening_events`; the map only name-drops "the listening-events recorder". If playback recording is another phase, the map should cross-reference it as a hard dependency.
- **`/api/auth/me` / `revalidateSession`** — cited repeatedly as the 401 recovery path, never specified as an endpoint.
- Minor: library "your year" block renders only `tracksPlayed` + `minutesListened` (+ journal/dna links); `topLanguage`/`likedCount`/`playlistCount` are returned by the summary endpoint but unused on that screen — map doesn't say which fields render.

All 16 named scope items are otherwise covered at depth and matched the code on inspection (incl. queue-drag constants 450ms/90px/16px, sleep presets 10/20/30/45/60 + end-of-set at `App.jsx:868`, TrackContextMenu base-item order/omit/extras, `?join=TOKEN` strip-before-accept, search trending).

## (2) Endpoint spot-checks — all verified correct, none wrong

1. `GET /api/home/quick-picks` — confirmed: salt sliced to 32 (`app.js:566`), response `{tracks, editionKey, cadence:'rotates daily', daypart}` (`quickPicks.js:152`), daypart boundaries 5/12/17/21, anchors top-3, exploration `'something new'`, reason strings and recently-played top-up exactly as mapped.
